title: Shortcut remapping for Keyboard Manager is not working

status.label: Awaiting the existing remap and docked-keyboard clarification
status.detail: A January 29, 2025 comment asks whether locking and unlocking restores the Win+Shift+S remap; a second commenter asks whether the issue occurs with a keyboard connected through a dock. Neither has a response from the reporter.

judgment.rationale: The report says Win+Shift+S is configured for no action but still opens the Windows screenshot UI, on PowerToys 0.87.1. A commenter asks whether locking and unlocking restores remapping, and another asks whether a keyboard connected through a dock is expected to work; neither question has an author response. Similar-issue bot suggestions do not establish coverage, and the separately referenced #35556 was closed as a duplicate of #32385, a broader Shift-state problem rather than this exact disabled-shortcut scenario.
evidence: The original report lists PowerToys 0.87.1 and says Win+Shift+S is configured for no action but still invokes the Windows screenshot shortcut.
A second commenter asks whether the mapping should work with a keyboard connected through a dock.
A January 29, 2025 commenter asks whether locking and unlocking restores the remap; no reporter response is present.
Issue #35556 was closed as a duplicate of #32385, which concerns Shift state becoming soft-deactivated and does not prove that the Win+Shift+S disabled mapping is covered.
judgment.recommended_action: Preserve the existing wait for the reporter to confirm whether lock/unlock restores the shortcut and whether the mapping is used on a docked keyboard; do not post a duplicate request.

fix_assessment.rationale: If current builds still pass Win+Shift+S through despite a no-action mapping, the OS may consume the reserved shortcut before Keyboard Manager suppresses it, or the mapping may not be applied to the active keyboard. Current behavior and dock/lock conditions need confirmation.

proposed_fixes.title: Suppress supported shortcuts mapped to no action
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The remapping pipeline may not suppress a reserved Win+Shift+S event before Windows invokes the screenshot UI, or the active keyboard may not receive the configured mapping.
plan: Check whether the existing mapping still reproduces on current stable and inspect the source/destination shown in the issue screenshot.
Test with the built-in keyboard and, if available, the dock-connected keyboard described by a commenter.
Check whether locking and unlocking restores the mapping, without treating that workaround as a permanent fix.
If the combination is supported, ensure the no-action mapping suppresses the OS action; otherwise present a clear reserved-shortcut limitation.
verification: Verify the configured no-action mapping prevents the screenshot UI on supported keyboards.
Verify mapping behavior after lock/unlock and after restarting PowerToys.
Verify other Win+Shift shortcuts are not unintentionally suppressed.

confidence.rationale: The failed Win+Shift+S behavior is specific, but current behavior, OS reservation constraints, and dock/lock conditions are unanswered.

issue_context.summary: Win+Shift+S reportedly still opens the Windows screenshot UI after Keyboard Manager maps it to no action.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.87.1 and includes a screenshot of the mapping.
The expected result is no action; the actual result is the Windows screenshot shortcut.
A commenter asks whether locking and unlocking restores the mapping; another asks about a dock-connected keyboard.
inferences: The OS may intercept the reserved shortcut before Keyboard Manager suppresses it, but this has not been demonstrated.
issue_context.analysis: The existing unanswered questions already request the discriminating lock/unlock and dock details. A maintainer can also reproduce the no-action mapping on current stable without posting a duplicate comment.
initial_investigation: Read the issue body and all comments, including the mapping screenshot reference and unanswered follow-ups.
Reviewed #35556 and #32385; the former is closed as a duplicate of the latter, which addresses a distinct soft-deactivated Shift symptom.

information_gaps.information: Whether lock/unlock restores the Win+Shift+S mapping and whether the same behavior occurs with a dock-connected keyboard on current stable
information_gaps.why_needed: These conditions distinguish an OS-reserved shortcut limitation from stale mapping state or an external-keyboard path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply to the existing comments with the current PowerToys version, whether Win+L followed by sign-in restores the mapping, and whether the failure occurs on the built-in and dock-connected keyboards.

actions.label: Reproduce Win+Shift+S no-action mapping
actions.note: The existing lock/unlock and docked-keyboard questions remain unanswered; do not post duplicates.

reproduce.title: Test the Win+Shift+S no-action mapping
setup: Use the mapping shown in the issue screenshot: map Win+Shift+S to no action.
steps: Press Win+Shift+S on the configured keyboard.
Repeat with a dock-connected keyboard if available.
Lock and unlock Windows, then test the mapping again.
reproduce.expected_result: The no-action mapping prevents the screenshot UI on supported keyboards and behaves consistently after lock/unlock.
